content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working with [product_name] [version_no] ([article_no]) and trying to build a FIFO-style analog register. Currently, I use a counter that resets every minute, and each reset should shift the counter value into a memory area (e.g., AM5), while previous values move to subsequent memory areas (AM7, AM8, etc.). My goal is to keep a rolling history of the last 10 minutes of counter data. Is this the correct way to achieve such functionality, or is there a more efficient method? Also, if the concept is valid, could you assist in making it work properly? My code works fine in the simulator, but in actual use, the memory areas fill randomly and inconsistently. Thank you very much, [user_name]

Thanks for the response. I'm a bit unsure now. Shouldn't Input I1 be responsible for loading values into the register, rather than acting as a reset? Also, B001 is supposed to function as the one-minute counter that triggers value shifting in the register, yet you've used it as a count trigger. Could you please explain how the mechanism is intended to operate? Thank you.

This is just a sample setup. A pulse generator sends a signal every 10 seconds, serving as the counting mechanism. When activated, it pushes values through the sequence of memory areas. The pulse initiates the process: first, the value moves from AM9 to AM10, then AM8 to AM9, AM7 to AM8, and so on. Ultimately, the current counter value is stored in AM1.
